function: Joint learned control of satellite-to-ground transmit power and bandwidth with DNN partition point and compute allocation, minimizing onboard energy while keeping task drops low in LEO inference offloading (pp. 8-9).
system: LEO satellite to one ground server downlink, LOS free-space path loss, 35 dB antenna gains (no array model), 12 GHz, 100 MHz, 20 W, no RIS (pp. 6, 12).
method: EG-PPO deep reinforcement learning (PPO with entropy regularization and GAE), actor with discrete and continuous heads, critic network; trained offline in simulation (pp. 9-12).
data_channel: Own simulator: LOS free-space path loss plus AWGN, LEO at 784 km, 12 GHz, parameters referenced to [15], [16]; no 3GPP model or measured data (pp. 6, 11-12).
test_conditions: 800 training episodes of 600 steps in the Table IV setup (p. 12); sweeps of task arrivals, bandwidth 50-300 MHz, compute 0.1-0.35 TFLOPS, DNN models; retraining unstated (pp. 13-16).
baselines: Greedy (GR); fixed partition points (FMP); ratio-based offloading (TRA, after [22]); learned SAC and DDQN with discretized allocation ratios (p. 12).
metrics: Task drop rate, total satellite energy, energy efficiency ratio (tasks per joule), average latency, total reward (Figs. 4-10, pp. 13-15).
complexity: Training O(N*T*[(K+1)F_pi+(M+1)F_V]); execution O(F_pi), one actor forward pass; no runtime or parameter count (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 6: "The communication between the LEO satellite and GS predominantly relies on Line-of-Sight (LOS) transmission links." The channel is a custom free-space path loss plus AWGN model (Eq. 6); no 3GPP TR 38.811 model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 12: "were trained for 800 episodes with 600 interaction steps per episode". Sweeps over task arrivals, bandwidth, compute and DNN models (pp. 13-16, p. 13: "we control per-slot task volume") never state that the trained agent is reused without retraining.
q3_support: p. 12: "FMP, TRA, GR, SAC, and DDQN exhibit 7.58%, 19.7%" (task drop rates; GR is a greedy rule, SAC and DDQN are learned baselines described on p. 12; energy efficiency ratio also compared in Figs. 5-10).
q4_support: p. 11: "the total computational complexity of Algorithm 1 is" O(N*T*[(K+1)F_pi+(M+1)F_V]) for training, and O(F_pi) for execution.
q5_support: p. 11: "The DRL algorithm was implemented using Python 3.9 and PyTorch 1.12.0 framework." No code or data link and no public channel dataset appear anywhere; the simulator is the authors' own.
notes: Included in area 6 by the satellite rule of Step 1: the DRL agent learns transmit power and bandwidth allocation of the LEO-ground link (physical layer) jointly with the DNN partition point and compute allocation (above the physical layer); p. 9: 'the satellite must jointly optimize a five-dimensional decision vector', which lists partitioning layers, onboard compute, transmit power, bandwidth and ground compute. Borderline for the reviewer: most of the paper is collaborative inference and offloading, which would be above_phy without the learned power and bandwidth. The link is one satellite to one ground server with antenna gains only, no MIMO and no RIS, which NTN admits. q2: no test of a trained agent in new conditions is stated, and the sweeps look like separate runs; reviewer to confirm. q3: p. 12 says all approaches were trained for 800 episodes and Fig. 4 (p. 13) shows learning curves for GR, FMP and TRA too, so the paper does not say how their allocations are computed; GR is non-learned only by its textual description as a greedy rule. PDF check: the first page holds the title 'Dynamic Collaborative Inference for Multi-Type DNN Tasks in Space-Ground Networks: A DRL Approach' and DOI 10.1109/TCCN.2025.3616114, which match the DOI of the work.
